title: Core: Add `getStoryHrefs` manager API and add hotkey for "open in isolation"
body:
## What I did

- Added `getStoryHrefs` method to `urls` manager API module
- Added keyboard shortcut for "open in isolation mode" (`Option-Shift-I` / `Alt-Shift-I`), using `api.getStoryHrefs`
- Updated preview iframe URL to use `api.getStoryHrefs`
- Updated `ShareMenu` component to use `api.getStoryHrefs` for all URLs, including QR code
- Deprecated old `getStoryHref` util in manager components
- Copied old `getStoryHref` into addon-docs source, because that's the only place it's still used and cannot be replaced with `api.getStoryHrefs` due to being in the preview. Yet another reason to not render docs pages in the preview.

## Checklist for Contributors

### Testing

#### Manual testing

1. Open a story, select a few globals (e.g. Grid and Viewport tools), and change some Controls to get args in the URL. Verify that the preview behaves accordingly.
2. Press Option-Shift-I (or Alt-Shift-I). This should open a new browser tab with the story preview (iframe.html). Verify that both globals and args are still applied.
3. Use the Share tool (top-right) to check the story link, isolation mode link and QR code to all link to the story correctly.
4. Navigate to a composed Storybook's story (setup composition if you have to) and check the same things. Globals should _not_ be carried over in isolation mode.

_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟠 Major_

**Missing URL encoding when building query parameters.**

Lines 10-12 construct the query string without URL-encoding the parameter values. While the `parseQuery` helper properly decodes parameters (line 21), the output construction doesn't encode them, which could cause issues with special characters in parameter values.



<details>
<summary>🔎 Proposed fix to add URL encoding</summary>

```diff
   return `${url}?${Object.entries(params)
-    .map((item) => `${item[0]}=${item[1]}`)
+    .map(([key, value]) => `${encodeURIComponent(key)}=${encodeURIComponent(value)}`)
     .join('&')}`;
```

This ensures proper encoding of special characters in both keys and values, consistent with the decoding in `parseQuery`.
</details>

<details>
<summary>🤖 Prompt for AI Agents</summary>

```
In code/addons/docs/src/blocks/getStoryHref.ts around lines 1 to 13, the
function builds the query string without URL-encoding keys or values; update the
query-string assembly to URL-encode both parameter names and values (e.g., use
encodeURIComponent on item[0] and item[1] or build the query with
URLSearchParams) so special characters are safely encoded when returning
`${url}?…`. Ensure the same ordering and inclusion of id and additionalParams
are preserved.
```

_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟡 Minor_

**Handle undefined ref gracefully.**

If `refId` is provided but `refs[refId]` is undefined (e.g., ref not loaded yet), `refs[refId]?.url` evaluates to `undefined`, resulting in `"undefined/iframe.html"` as the preview base URL.

<details>
<summary>🔎 Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
-      const previewBase = refId
-        ? refs[refId]?.url + '/iframe.html'
+      const refUrl = refId ? refs[refId]?.url : undefined;
+      const previewBase = refUrl
+        ? refUrl + '/iframe.html'
         : global.PREVIEW_URL || `${managerBase}iframe.html`;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary>🤖 Prompt for AI Agents</summary>

```
In code/core/src/manager-api/modules/url.ts around lines 246 to 248,
constructing previewBase uses refs[refId]?.url which can be undefined and
produces "undefined/iframe.html"; change the logic to only use refs[refId].url
when refs[refId] exists and has a url, otherwise fall back to global.PREVIEW_URL
or managerBase; implement this by testing refs[refId]?.url (or using nullish
coalescing e.g. (refs[refId]?.url ?? global.PREVIEW_URL ?? managerBase) +
'/iframe.html') so the final previewBase never contains "undefined".
```

</details>

comments.author: coderabbitai
comments.body:
_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟡 Minor_

**Handle colons in serialized parameter values.**

`split(':')` splits on every colon occurrence. If a value contains colons (e.g., `"theme:dark:blue"`), the destructuring `[key, value]` only captures the first two segments, discarding the rest. This could cause data loss when merging args or globals that have colon-separated values.



<details>
<summary>🔎 Proposed fix using split with limit</summary>

```diff
 const parseSerializedParam = (param: string) =>
   Object.fromEntries(
     param
       .split(';')
-      .map((pair) => pair.split(':'))
+      .map((pair) => pair.split(':', 2))
       .filter(([key, value]) => key && value)
   );
```

This limits the split to at most 2 parts, preserving colons in the value.

</details>

<!-- suggestion_start -->

<details>
<summary>📝 Committable suggestion</summary>

> ‼️ **IMPORTANT**
> Carefully review the code before committing. Ensure that it accurately replaces the highlighted code, contains no missing lines, and has no issues with indentation. Thoroughly test & benchmark the code to ensure it meets the requirements.

```suggestion
const parseSerializedParam = (param: string) =>
  Object.fromEntries(
    param
      .split(';')
      .map((pair) => pair.split(':', 2))
      .filter(([key, value]) => key && value)
  );
```

</details>

<!-- suggestion_end -->

<details>
<summary>🤖 Prompt for AI Agents</summary>

```
In code/core/src/manager-api/modules/url.ts around lines 35 to 41, the parsing
logic uses pair.split(':') which splits on every colon and loses parts when
values contain colons; change the split to limit to two parts (e.g.,
pair.split(':', 2)) so the first segment is the key and the remainder (including
any colons) is the value, keep the existing filter for truthy key/value and
preserve Object.fromEntries usage.
```

</details>

This function used to be defined (and still is only for backwards compat) in `storybook/internal/components`.

This seemed not the right place, but removal is a backwards incompatible change, so we duplicated the code into addon-docs to remove usage, to make the removal easier, hopefully by SB11.

comments.author: Sidnioulz
comments.body:
We do have rather inconsistent usage of this stringify util. In some code paths, we ensure it supports nesting, and in others, we don't.

This is what router utils use which I believe we should align with:
```ts
  return stringify(encodeSpecialValues(object), {
    delimiter: ';', // we don't actually create multiple query params
    nesting: true,
    nestingSyntax: 'js', // encode objects using dot notation: obj.key=val
  })
```

Ideally we'd call this directly: https://github.com/storybookjs/storybook/blob/next/code/core/src/router/utils.ts#L186-L214; if not possible we should ensure logics are identical.

comments.author: ndelangen
comments.body: We should be able to use it, I think.

comments.author: ghengeveld
comments.body: I don't think the `;` delimiter makes sense for custom query params. Those should just be actual query params, delimited by `&`, I think that's what users would expect. The other options are good but that's already how it works currently.

comments.author: Sidnioulz
comments.body:
@ghengeveld you're right, I jumped to conclusions a little. We do only want to call those options for args. I can see that the code that merges serialized params is completely agnostic to args specifics, and so manages to preserve both encoded special values and the `;` delimiter for multiple args.

I'll add sanity checks for specially encoded values in the tests and add the `nesting`/`nestingSyntax` options so the code is more explicit. I think we would do users a service if we used the same nesting syntax throughout args/globals/custom params though so I'll align on `js`.

**Guard against undefined `storyId` in copyStoryLink.**

The `copyStoryLink` handler calls `getStoryHrefs(storyId, { refId })` without verifying that `storyId` is defined, unlike the similar `openInIsolation` handler which guards with `if (storyId && viewMode === 'story')`. When triggered on settings or about pages where `storyId` is undefined, this results in a malformed URL (e.g., `?path=/story/undefined`) being copied to the clipboard.

<details>
<summary>🔎 Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
 case 'copyStoryLink': {
+  if (!storyId) {
+    break;
+  }
   const { managerHref } = fullAPI.getStoryHrefs(storyId, { refId });
   copy(managerHref);
   break;
 }
```
</details>
